title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

reports.title: US woman falsely charged with bank theft sues for $10m over AI facial recognition

summary:
Angela Lipps, a 50-year-old Tennessee woman, was arrested at gunpoint in July 2025 and spent about six months in jail after police in Fargo, North Dakota wrongly used AI facial recognition to link her to bank fraud. She faced four counts of unauthorized use of personal identifying information and four counts of theft, but the charges were dropped when her lawyer provided bank records showing she was in Tennessee at the time. Lipps had never been to North Dakota and did not look like the suspect in surveillance footage.

Lipps is now suing the city of Fargo and detective Lucas Heck for $10 million, claiming false arrest, malicious prosecution, and a lack of police training or supervision on facial recognition technology. She says she lost her home, car, and personal property, and was denied medications and dentures while in custody. The city declined to comment on pending litigation. The lawsuit seeks accountability and hopes to encourage officers to use more care with AI facial recognition.
